steps.title: Reds
steps.body: Blaufränkisch is the signature: dark cherry, blackberry, pepper and spice, with fresh acidity and firm tannin. Zweigelt, Austria's most planted red, a 1922 cross of Blaufränkisch and St. Laurent, gives soft, cherry reds. St. Laurent gives Pinot-like elegance. Pinot Noir, Merlot and Cabernet also appear in blends.

steps.title: Whites
steps.body: Welschriesling, unrelated to Riesling, is widely grown, especially for sweet wines. Chardonnay, locally Morillon in parts of Austria, Pinot Blanc, Grüner Veltliner and Furmint, revived near Rust, also grow here. Sweet wines often blend several white grapes affected by noble rot.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.
steps.explanation: Burgenland grows reds and sweet whites.

steps.body: Welschriesling has nothing to do with Riesling. Despite the name, they're not related.
